nodes.label: TSH 6.8
nodes.summary: Thyroid-stimulating hormone above range: the pituitary is pushing a sluggish thyroid. A single reading is not a diagnosis — it needs a free T4 and a repeat in six to eight weeks.

affects.how: a slow thyroid lowers heart rate and raises LDL

nodes.label: ALT 71
nodes.summary: Alanine aminotransferase about 1.7× the upper limit. It points at the liver, not at the muscle, but it says nothing about the cause: fat, alcohol, drugs and viral hepatitis all look like this. An ultrasound and a repeat in three months separate them.

affects.how: hepatocyte injury; if fat-driven, it can progress to fibrosis
fatty liver travels with insulin resistance and higher CV risk

nodes.label: Blood pressure 135/90
nodes.summary: Monthly average of daily home readings: 135/90. That is stage 1 hypertension — the diastolic is the louder number here. Home averages beat a single office reading, which is why this one is kept as a document rather than a note.

affects.how: higher afterload: left ventricle thickens, then stiffens
raised pressure filters harder; nephrons scar silently
small-vessel disease: white-matter change, later vascular dementia
hypertensive retinopathy — the only place the damage is visible

nodes.label: Blood pressure 150/110
nodes.summary: Monthly average of daily home readings: 150/110. Stage 2 hypertension, and 110 diastolic is the part that buys damage — it is the pressure the heart has to push against between beats. Two years after 135/90 this is progression, not a bad day.

affects.how: concentric hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction; LVH on echo
glomerular pressure injury; albumin in the urine is the first sign
stroke risk roughly doubles per 20 mmHg systolic
wall stress: aneurysm and dissection risk climb
flame haemorrhages and papilloedema at this level

nodes.label: Glucose 4.94
nodes.summary: Fasting glucose 4.94 mmol/l, mid-range. It says the pancreas is keeping up today; it does not say what happens after a meal. HbA1c is the number that answers that.

affects.how: beta cells are meeting demand — no sign of strain
normal fasting glucose keeps the metabolic CV risk low

nodes.label: Lipid panel
nodes.summary: Four markers from one draw. LDL is 4.2 mmol/l — 1.4× the upper limit and the number that builds plaque; triglycerides are up too, which usually means the liver is making more fat than it burns. HDL is the one still doing its job. This is not tomorrow, but the clock is running.

affects.how: LDL deposits in the arterial wall; the total burden over decades is what counts
raised triglycerides travel with fat in the liver
very high triglycerides can inflame the pancreas; 2.4 is far from that

nodes.label: hyperlipidaemia
nodes.text: Mixed hyperlipidaemia. LDL 4.2 mmol/l with triglycerides at 2.4. With the blood pressure at 150/110 last month this is not a number to watch for a year: the ten-year risk puts this patient over the threshold where a statin is worth it. Start atorvastatin 20 mg in the evening, repeat the panel in three months, and bring the home blood-pressure diary to the next visit. Alcohol down to two units a week. Walk thirty minutes, five days a week.
nodes.summary: A cardiologist read the November panel together with the October blood pressure and put this patient over the risk threshold: a statin, a repeat panel in three months, and the non-drug half of the plan.

nodes.label: possible iron deficiency
nodes.text: Generated from the November panel. Haemoglobin at the bottom of the range with a low-ish MCV — a pattern that fits iron deficiency, and also fits thalassaemia trait. Ferritin separates them; it is not in this document.
nodes.summary: Haemoglobin is at the bottom of the range and the MCV is low-ish. That pattern is where iron deficiency usually starts, but a low-ish MCV also happens with thalassaemia trait. Ferritin is the test that separates them, and this document does not have one.

nodes.label: atorvastatin 20 mg in the evening
nodes.text: Start it after the evening meal. The note also asks for the home blood-pressure diary at the next visit.

nodes.label: repeat the lipid panel in three months
nodes.text: A repeat panel after twelve weeks of treatment, to see whether the statin moved LDL.

nodes.label: cut saturated fat, two units of alcohol a week
nodes.text: Saturated fat down. The note sets alcohol at two units a week.

nodes.label: walk thirty minutes, five days a week
nodes.text: Thirty minutes, five days a week. The note does not name a pace or a heart-rate target.

nodes.label: no more than two units a week
nodes.text: The note sets the weekly limit but does not say what counts as a unit.

nodes.label: red yeast rice, twice a day
nodes.text: Red yeast rice carries the same active compound as a statin, without the dose control of a prescribed one.

nodes.label: hypertension, stage 1
nodes.summary: A doctor's note after the October home readings: stage 1 hypertension. It is a diagnosis, not a measurement — the note holds what was decided next, and the later 150/110 shows this one did not hold.

nodes.label: home blood-pressure diary
nodes.summary: Two weeks of twice-daily home readings before any drug, so the number that gets treated is the average and not one nervous morning in a clinic.

nodes.label: 2025 in one page
plan: a lipid panel once in the year
the home blood-pressure diary kept twice a day
fact: no lipid panel was done in 2025
two blood-pressure averages were brought to the clinic, four months apart
held: the diary was kept through the spring
dropped: the annual lipid panel never happened — which is why the November 2026 panel reads as a step change

nodes.label: repeat blood pressure check
nodes.summary: Planned check after the stage 2 reading: a repeat average and a decision on treatment. Planned is not done — until it happens this row is a plan, not a record.
